references.text: Jeremiah warns against false prophets who speak lies in the Lord's name, which corresponds to the test for false prophets in Deuteronomy.
The Lord condemns prophets who prophesy lies in His name and declares that He has not sent them; they speak false visions and deception.
God says He did not send these false prophets, yet they ran and spoke in His name without His command.
Ezekiel warns against prophets who see false visions and prophesy lies, yet say, 'Thus says the Lord,' even though the Lord has not sent them.
The prophets cover over with whitewash, see false visions, and prophesy lies, saying, 'Thus says the Lord God,' when the Lord has not spoken.
Micah condemns prophets who lead the people astray and prophesy for payment, warning that they will be put to shame when their visions do not come true.
Zechariah prophesies about a time when anyone who speaks lies in a prophetic spirit will be punished for speaking lies in the Lord's name.
Jesus warns against false prophets and says they are known by their fruits—a test that aligns with Deuteronomy's criterion that prophecies must come to pass.
Jesus warns that many false prophets will arise and lead many astray in the last days.
Jesus warns that false messiahs and false prophets will appear and perform great signs and wonders to deceive even the elect.
John urges believers to test the spirits to see if they are from God, because many false prophets have gone out into the world.
